title: Maltitol: what it means for your plan
standfirst: Which of our plan rules this ingredient turns on, and what that does not tell you.

spans.text: Maltitol is a sugar alcohol (polyol) used as a reduced-calorie sweetener that tastes similar to sugar. It is made by hydrogenating maltose from starch.
Why it is in your food
Manufacturers use maltitol as a sweetener and it is of plant origin.
Our scorer looks for maltitol when Low-FODMAP is on for you. If that plan is off, your score does not change. This is how the app reads a label. It is not a claim about health.
One word on a label can cover more than one thing. A plan may also turn on how much is in the food, which this page cannot see. Read the pack when it matters.
